access.fees: None — no climbing fee (National Forest, not Mount Rainier NP)
access.notes: Many of these peaks (Mount Persis, Gunn Peak, Baring Mountain area) sit outside designated wilderness — administratively unrestricted despite serious technical terrain.
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.

routes.best_season: Late July through September for the snow-free rock route; the same buttress is also climbed as a winter ice/mixed line (roughly WI2-3) from about December through March when it's in condition.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July through September for dry rock conditions (best in August); the same buttress line also forms a separate winter alpine ice/mixed objective when consolidated

May.reason: Snow climb/avalanche terrain; not a rock or reliable ice season

July.reason: Route typically dries out by mid-to-late July; some early-season snow patches possible on approach

June.reason: Approach gully and lower buttress often still hold snow/ice; not yet a dry rock route

April.reason: Spring transition - rising avalanche and wet-slide hazard, deteriorating ice

March.reason: Late winter ice can still be in condition, but spring warming begins increasing hazard

August.reason: Best window for dry rock; most stable weather of the summer

January.reason: Core winter ice season when conditions are in and avalanche hazard is manageable

October.reason: Early snow/wet weather can arrive; shorter daylight window

December.reason: Winter ice/mixed conditions can come in; requires stable, consolidated ice

November.reason: Transitional season - unstable early-season snowpack, not yet a reliable ice route

September.reason: Still generally dry with cooler temps; days shortening

days.note: A popular moderate alpine rock outing from the Alpental upper lot: approach past Source Lake into the basin, then climb 4-5 pitches of easy class 3-4 rock with big exposure up the buttress to the summit. Descent is via rappel/downclimb to the standard route and back down the approach.
days.title: Car-to-car: approach, climb the Northeast Buttress, descend

schedule.label: Leave Alpental upper parking lot
schedule.detail: Headlamp start; snow travel to Source Lake and the basin is common outside of summer.

schedule.label: Reach base of the Northeast Buttress
schedule.detail: One detailed trip report logged 3 hr 24 min car-to-base.

schedule.label: Climb the buttress (4-5 pitches, class 3-4)
schedule.detail: Same report logged 2 hr 39 min base-to-summit.

schedule.label: Summit (6,238 ft)
schedule.detail: Brief stop for views/food before starting down.

schedule.label: Rappel/downclimb back to base of climb
schedule.detail: Reverses onto the standard route rather than down the buttress itself.

schedule.label: Descend to car
schedule.detail: Retrace the approach back to the Alpental lot.

days.objective: Summit Chair Peak via the Northeast Buttress

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car, about 10-12 hours; one well-documented trip logged 11 hr 22 min total with roughly 3,100 ft of gain over the round trip.
